title: Protected: Bon Voyage Waterford-Dublin Bound!
author: tharrison
content_raw:
Hello Irish Life Experience Families and Friends!  I’m back and my computer is fixed, so hopefully my posts will be more regular.  We arrived to Dublin today and are getting settled in our new home of King’s Hospital tonight.  Just a little update from the past few days, before I report to you on today.    
All of the students loved their time in Waterford, but they have been looking forward to exploring a new home.  “Waterford was a small enough city where you got to know where everything was and it felt like home,” Paddy said.  “I loved it here,” said Savannah. 
A few highlights of Monday’s and Wednesday’s classes and workshops.
Monday morning, the ILE went to the new Waterford Crystal Factory for a quick tour.  It reopened two weeks ago, and is superb.  Students saw the process of blowing Waterford Crystal and the time and detail that goes into each piece.  They were very careful not to break anything:).  
In literature, Angie did more readings from Ulysses, while Pete spoke about Patrick Kavanagh.  Pete said Patrick Kavanagh is one of his favorite Irish writers, so he was excited to share his knowledge with the students.  
Dan touched upon the 1916 Rebellion in Irish history and the famine in Irish American history.  Katie said Dan is a wonderful teacher and is very knowledgeable.  
Taryn decided to try her skills in Gaelic and taught the students a few colors, right and left, and hand and foot, so they could play a game of Irish Twister.  It was hilarious!   
In her Irish studies class, Taryn gave a quiz of Irish counties.  All of the students did fantastic.  Paddy and Savannah studied very hard and received a perfect score.  Way to go!  They will be receiving a special prize from Taryn for their hard efforts. 
Siobhan treated the students to a DVD of her great uncle, Ernie O’Malley.  Ernie O’Malley was born in Castlebar, County Mayo, Ireland.  He was an Irish Republican Army officer during the Irish War of Independence and a commander of the anti-treaty IRA during the Irish Civil War.  Piper said she thought the documentary on Ernie O’Malley was very interesting.    
After the classes on Monday, students had the option of taking a Scone Baking Workshop.  Dan and Taryn taught them how to make delicious scones, so hopefully they will be trying their culinary skills on you during St. Patrick’s Day next year.  The scones turned out wonderfully and the students were able to sample them during evening tea.  Hannah said they tasted delicious, but the next time she wanted to add Craisins to them and try them with jam or jelly. 
In the evening, Pete and Siobhan arranged a game of Capture the Flag with the students and they took it very seriously.  As you can see from the pictures, they dressed up in their team colors and even painted their faces.  The game lasted a few hours, before Siobhan called it a tie.
During Wednesday afternoon, the students were required to take a mandatory workshop of Gaelic football and hurling, by Waterford GAA Coach, Eoin Breathnach.  Eoin was very impressed by the athleticism of our ILE students.  He was amazed how fast they were able to pick up the sports.  Clara and Paddy had a natural talent for Gaelic football, since they have both played soccer.  Maureen said she loved Gaelic football, but found hurling very challenging.  
Later that evening, Eoin invited the ILE students to a Cork vs. Waterford hurling game.  What a blast!  The ILE students cheered for Waterford and sported their blue and white county colors.  What spirit!  Cork put up a good fight, but Waterford won in the end.  Up Waterford!  “I enjoyed learning how to play hurling and then being able to watch it,” said Sydney.  
Tuesday marked our final tour day in Waterford to Cahir Castle, the Blarney Castle, Cork, and a quick stop in Youghal.  
Once the stronghold of the powerful Butler family, the Cahir Castle retains its impressive keep, tower and much of its original defensive structure.  It is one of Ireland’s largest and best preserved castles. It is situated on a rocky island on the River Suir.  After a short tour, students were able to explore all of the nooks and cranny’s of Cahir Castle.  Piper said she really liked the tour and learned a lot.  
Then we were off to Blarney.  Blarney Castle was built nearly six hundred years ago by one of Ireland’s greatest chieftains, Cormac MacCarthy, and has been attracting attention beyond Munster ever since.  Over the last few hundred years, millions have flocked to Blarney, making it a world landmark and one of Ireland’s greatest treasures.
Now that might have something to do with the Blarney Stone, the legendary Stone of Eloquence, found at the top of the Tower.  Kiss it and you’ll never again be lost for words.  There were a handful of students that now have the “Gift of the Gab”-not that many of them need it;).  
As you can see, the students are learning A LOT about Ireland.  They are soaking it all in and becoming more passionate about Irish culture with each passing day.  I’m so proud of them all!

title: Protected: Happy 4th of July!
author: tharrison
content_raw:
While there were no fireworks or sparklers, the Irish Life Experience had an exceptional 4th of July in Ireland!  
We were able to have a lie-in yesterday and catch up on much needed beauty sleep.  It was glorious.  A few students attended an Irish Mass at the local church and said it was very similar to a US service, except the Priest spoke much faster.  After our relaxing morning, we were treated to a traditional Irish breakfast/brunch at Newtown Boarding School.  Students sampled Irish pancakes, rashers, sausages, and even black pudding.  A lot of them devoured the black pudding, so I didn’t dare tell them what was in it;).  Shhh!
The morning was a little dreary with a few scattered showers.  However, by the time we departed Newtown for Tramore-a popular seaside town in Co. Waterford-the clouds pushed away.  We were graced with sunshine once again.  It was perfect weather for a beach day. 
We got to Tramore and there were a few brave souls who decided to go swimming.  Burrr!  Maureen dunked her head in almost immediately and swam for a few minutes.  What a thrill.  Many just waded out into the blustery waves-feeling the cold temperature of the water was enough for them.  Katie said she loved the sand run through her feet for the first time.  
Others walked along the beach, while a handful played a game of volleyball with the Staff.  Shortly thereafter, a group decided to go on the amusement park rides.  Between the Twister and the Whirly Twirly, there were plenty of screams and yelps from the Irish Life Experience.  It was very exhilarating.  We ended the rides with 99’s-scrumptious ice-cream in Ireland.  
A lot of students relaxed on the beach soaking in Ireland.  Before we knew it, we had to leave Tramore with quite a few sunburns in tow.  
We got back to Newtown Boarding School and an American barbeque awaited us.  Hamburgers and french fries galore.  Afterwards, Pete-Counselor Extraordinaire-arranged an activity for the students.  Everyone participated in his Counselor Olympics, which included dizzy bat, egg and spoon, and wheelbarrow relays, along with a water balloon toss.  The Yeats’ group was successful and managed to pull out a win.
The night concluded with an American movie and a pizza party- complete with candy, soda, and popcorn.  A little taste of home away from home.  Caitlyn said it was a perfect way to celebrate the 4th of July.  
The incredible Counselor, Siobhan, said, “there was plenty of red, white, and blue amidst the green, white, and orange yesterday.  However, after the gorgeous weather, many students came back with even more red.”  We will have to remember sunscreen the next beautiful day at the beach.
Looking back, Saturday was a typical class day.  Students finished up learning about Joyce and did readings from Ulysses in Angie’s literature class.  Dan taught the students how to ask each other out on dates in Gaelic, which he said was highly entertaining.  In Irish history, the students learned about Cromwell and plantations.  From around 1200 to 1700.  Taryn focused on genealogy with the students and how to trace their roots back to Ireland.  They also learned about their families Coat of Arms, which Piper said she really enjoyed.  In the last class of Irish American history, Dan spoke about the Scott’s Irish and what they did in America.  
In the afternoon, students had the option of doing a St. Brigid’s Cross Workshop and a Celtic Picture Frame Workshop.  
Brigid’s crosses are associated with Brigid of Kildare, who is venerated as one of the patron saints of Ireland.  The crosses are traditionally made on February 1st-on St. Brigid’s Feast Day.  This Feast coincides with the more ancient one of her pagan namesake, one of pagan Ireland’s most important Goddesses, Brigid, who is associated with fire, healing and holy wells; it celebrates the earliest stirrings of Spring, and is called Imbolc.
Many rituals are associated with the making of the crosses.  It was traditionally believed that a Brigid’s Cross protects the house from fire and evil.  It is hung in many Irish and Irish-American kitchens for this purpose, so I’m sure a few students will bring their crosses home to hang up in their kitchens.  
Saturday was busy day and we ended the evening with a venture into town to check out a local festival, followed by a mandatory movie of Michael Collins.  
All is wonderful with the Irish Life Experience.  The students are happy as clams and are doing well.  The Staff adores them all.  They are such a great bunch of kids!  
Families and friends, feel free to comment.  Students are following along and would love to hear from you all.

title: Protected: Cashels and Castles
author: tharrison
content_raw:
Hello Irish Life Experience Families and Friends!  Yesterday, we had the opportunity to travel to the Rock of Cashel and Kilkenny Castle.  The weather, AGAIN was in our favor.  The sun shone most of the day and we were only caught in a few sprinkles of showers.  It was gorgeous for the majority of the tour and we couldn’t have lucked out more.  
For those of you who are unfamiliar with the Rock of Cashel, it’s huge, it’s complex, it’s iconic, and there is nothing like it anywhere
else in the world!  It’s in the heart of Tipperary.  The Rock of Cashel-Carraig Phádraig, more formally known as St. Patrick’s Rock or the Cashel of the Kings.  Reputedly the site of the conversion of Aenghus the King of Munster by St. Patrick in the 5th century AD.  Long before the Norman invasion The Rock of Cashel was the seat of the High Kings of Munster, although there is little structural evidence of their time here.  Most of the buildings on the current site date from the 12th and 13th centuries when the rock was gifted to the Church.  The buildings represent both Hiberno-Romanseque and Germanic influences in their architecture.
The complex has a character of its own, unique and native, and is one of the most remarkable collections of Celtic art and medieval architecture to be found anywhere in Europe.
Students were able to explore the Rock and take some gorgeous pictures of views and the fortress itself.  It was spectacular.  
Afterwards, the Irish Life Experience marched onwards to Kilkenny Castle.  Here we enjoyed our packed lunches on the lush green grounds.  Students were introduced to the Hula Hoop Challenge.  The Challenge is simple-placing delicious chip-like Hula Hoops on fingers and gobbling them one-by-one as fast as you can.  Caitlin ended up being the Grand Champion, but Siobhan proved to be strong competition.  
On full stomachs, we then went on a tour of the Castle.  The Castle stands dramatically on a strategic height that commands a crossing on the River Nore and dominates Kilkenny City.  Over the eight centuries of its existence, many additions and alterations have been made to the fabric of the building, making Kilkenny Castle today a complex structure of various architectural styles.
The original Anglo-Norman stone castle was built for William Marshal, 4th Earl of Pembroke (c.1146-1219) during the first decade of the  thirteenth century.  Kilkenny Castle later became the principal Irish residence of the powerful Butler family for almost 600 years.  The Butler ownership began when James (c.1360-1405), 3rd Earl of Ormond, purchased the castle in c.1391, and lasted until 1967 when Arthur, 6th Marquess of Ormonde (1893-1971), presented it to the people of Kilkenny in return for a token payment of £50.  Can you believe that???
Scarlett said she enjoyed one of the tour guides and his hearty laugh.  She also liked the giant toilet off of one of the rooms.  Other students loved the gardens in the front of the Castle and we spent quite some time taking pictures together.  Caitlin was very impressed.  Her family have traced their roots back to the Butler family, so this tour was extremely special to Caitlin.  
We gave the students some time to enjoy the city of Kilkenny, before we went back to Waterford.  They had a blast meandering their way throughout the cobblestone streets and shopping for souvenirs.  
Later that evening, all of the students joined a soccer game on Newtown’s pitch in honor of the World Cup games we have been following.  There were a few players of the game…  Clara had two goals, Caitlin and Joe collided together twice in a rush for the ball, and Caitlyn proved to be a strong Goalie-saving three kicks!  
To finish up the day, we played Assassins-a fun murder mystery game.  We discovered that Maureen and Clara were excellent at convincing everyone they weren’t the killers-when in fact they were.
Once again, another spectacular day!  All of the students are happy and doing well.  Enjoy the pictures.  They are ALL so photogenic!

title: Protected: Wonderful Waterford
author: tharrison
content_raw:
Since we have arrived in Ireland, the weather has been absolutely gorgeous.  Maureen said the sunshine makes it perfect to walk around and explore Waterford.  We luckily haven’t had to use our raincoats once.  Hopefully, I didn’t just jinx us.  
Yesterday commenced the first day of classes for the Irish Life Experience.  The students woke up bright and early for breakfast-feeling rejuvenated after a long two days of traveling.  All of the students seem to have adjusted well to Irish time and have fully recovered from their jet leg.
Many were looking forward to learning more about Irish culture, so yesterday and today were a wonderful introduction.  
Angie talked about the history of Irish literature in her first class.  Today, she touched upon James Joyce and gave them an explanation of Ulysses.  Riley said she learned a lot, because she had never heard of James Joyce before.
In Gaelic, Dan gave the students a background into Gaelic language.  Savannah said that that she learned the following Gaelic phrases:  Hello-Dia Dhuit, How are you?-Conas atá tú?, _____is anim dom.-My name is_____.  Dakota and Hannah said Gaelic is their favorite class, because they enjoy learning new languages.  “I love Dan,” said Hannah.  
In Irish history, Dan gave the students background into the Pre-History of Ireland.  He spoke about the Celts to St. Patrick and St. Patrick to Strongbow.  Strongbow is significant, because Christ Church Cathedral in Waterford is where he married the Irish Princess Aoife, daughter of the King of Leinster in 1170 AD.  Many of students will be able to visit the Christ Church Cathedral firsthand while they are in Waterford this week, so it is a nice connection to their history class.  
Taryn taught the students about the Geography and Geology of Ireland, and today discussed the Counties and Provinces of Ireland.  She spiced up the class with a few jokes and some fun facts of Ireland, which the students did not find quite as amusing;).  Joke:  How do you know an Irishman is having a good time?  Answer:  He’s Dublin over with laughter.  
In Irish American History, students shared their Irish roots and how their families came to America.  Caryl, Clara, Hannah, and Maureen told the other students about their grandparents and great-grandparents from Ireland.  They also talked about some of the reasons why people emigrated to America.  
In the evenings, students participated in drama and dance.  In drama they are working on limericks for the week of famous historical figures in Ireland.  The limericks will be judged and the winner will receive a prize.  In dance, the amazing Siobhan demonstrated the Siege of Ennis.  The students learned the steps very quickly with the help of Hannah and Scarlett.  We were also lucky enough to have them show us their talent.  Very impressive!  
Tonight, students participated in Siobhan’s Digital Scavenger Hunt.  They were split into groups and had to find things that totaled 800 points.  A few of the things on the list were:  A Red Door=10 Points, A Photo in Front of Dominos=15 Points, A Photo of a Hurling Stick in Action=25 Points, A Photo of a Pub or Storefront with a Group Member’s Name=50 Points, and A Photo of a Squirrel=100 Points.  The Pickled Onion Team (Hannah, PK-AKA Paddy, Riley, Savannah, and Scarlett) successfully won with a picture of a squirrel on a cereal box.  This was a hard one.  The kids had to get creative, because there are no squirrels in Ireland;).  
The night ended with an impromptu music sessiun by Pete serenading the students with a few Irish tunes from Paul Brady.  
It has been a great few days!  We are off to Kilkenny Castle and the Rock of Cashel tomorrow.  …More to come over the next few days.

title: Protected: Fáilte go hÉirinn!
author: tharrison
content_raw:
Hello Family and Friends of the 2010 Irish Life Experience Participants!  Just a quick update to let you know we have arrived safe and sound to the Emerald Isle.  
The majority of Monday was spent at JFK International Airport meeting and greeting 2010 Irish Life Experience Participants and their parents.  We had quite a few students arriving from connecting flights, throughout the day.  The earliest was Katie, from Montana, at 6:00 AM.  Katie said she had a blast flying and seeing the ocean for the first time in her life. The majority of other students arrived in the evening, as our flight did not take off until 9:50 PM.  Needless to say, it was a tiring, yet exciting day for all.  A big shout out to Sydney and her parents, from Kansas for all of their hard work and patience.  Sydney had numerous delays and made our Aer Lingus flight with a mad dash through terminals and five minutes to spare!  What a champ!
The Aer Lingus flight was very smooth and comfortable.  No turbulence.  We lucked out with a new airplane and the students passed their time by watching a variety of movies and playing numerous games on their own personal TV’s.  What a treat.  A few students managed to get some shut eye, but many were too excited in anticipation of arriving to Ireland.  
We landed at Dublin Airport almost an hour before our scheduled time, breezed through Customs and met our two incredible Irish teachers, Angie and Dan.  We collected our luggage and boarded the bus to set off for our new home for the next nine days-Newtown Boarding School.  
It was a gorgeous day, so we broke up the four hour drive to Waterford with a stop at Glendalough in the Wicklow Mountains.  The students learned from Dan that Glendalough means ‘valley of two lakes.’  Glendalough is a world famous Monastic Site with a Round Tower and many scenic lakes.  We stretched our legs, got some fresh air, posed for pictures, and walked around the Lower Lake-all while soaking up the Irish sun.  Caitlyn W. said it was absolutely beautiful.  Many of the girls were also excited to learn that parts of the recent movie, Leap Year, were filmed at Glendalough.  After getting our exercise, we enjoyed a packed lunch of ham sandwiches, fruit, a Mars Bar, and crisps-which are chips in Ireland.  PK said it was a nice break to have a picnic in the park.  
After our tour of Glendalough, we continued on our journey.  We got to Waterford two hours later, got settled, freshened up, and had tea.  An Orientation of the Program and Ice-Breakers were next on the agenda.  After a few games of getting to know one another, we watched the Portugal vs. Spain game of the World Cup.  Most of the students cheered for Portugal, but Spain pulled off a win 1-0.  
Students retired to bed after the game around 9:00 PM.  Many were jet legged and have never been so excited to go to bed.  They were all in good spirits, but extremely exhausted.
Thank you so much to everyone!  It was wonderful to finally meet all of the students and their families at JFK.  
An absolutely perfect start to the first day of the 2010 Irish Life Experience.

title: Protected: Introducing Your 2010 Female Counselor
author: tharrison
content_raw: Siobhán Kennedy here from Winchester, MA, eager and excited to spend an unforgettable summer in Ireland!  I am a recent graduate from Providence College with a degree in English and secondary studies in Sociology and Business.  As the youngest of three girls in a pure-bred Irish household, I am the last of the Kennedy Clan to join Taryn as a Counselor after following her through the cobbles, cottages, and peat on my own summer excursion across the pond in 2005.  In my junior year I studied abroad in Stellenbosch, South Africa, and though it wasn’t Waterford, Dublin, or Galway, I still had the time of my life.  On top of my studying in Stellenbosch, I coached a boy’s High School basketball team and was a pre-primary school teacher’s assistant in the Kayamandi Township.  Living in the heart of the winelands of South Africa, I quickly jumped on board with the University’s Wine Society all in the name of cultural immersion.  After Ireland, I intend to cash in on my Irish passport and move to Australia for a few years and let the US economy right itself while I’m away.  I cannot wait to meet what will be a stellar group this summer.  Let the adventure begin!

title: Protected: Introducing Your 2010 Male Counselor
author: tharrison
content_raw: Hi there!  My name is Pete Ford and I am originally from Glen Mills, PA, but have been living in North Jersey for the past twelve years.  I went to Ithaca College for my B.A. in English, and recently graduated from Seton Hall University with a Masters in English.  Aside from my obvious interest in literature and writing, I am a dedicated musician.  I play primarily banjo and guitar, but I will not hesitate to doodle on other stringed thingies.  I have been trying to install myself in the North Jersey Irish sessiun scene since I moved back in the winter of ’09, and it has been a worthwhile and rollicking good time.  I also teach banjo and guitar, and have done so since I was in high school.  I really love to teach, and hope to do so in the classroom some day.  I went to Ireland with Taryn as a student in 2002, and then as a Counselor in 2008 and 2009, and absolutely loved ALL trips.  I am understandably excited to go back again this year and meet all the new students, though they probably don’t know that they are in for the trip of a lifetime.  See you folks in a few weeks!

title: Past Testimonials
author: tharrison
content_raw:
While they probably feel old by now, we still love them and just can’t bring ourselves to replace the valuable testimonials from those below!

When Taryn asked me to share my thoughts about the Irish Life Experience program, I was stumped. I had no idea where to start! So many memories were made, laughs shared, and friendships born, that will last forever. I laugh every time I think of my attempt at playing rugby and Gaelic football, not to mention hurling! We were able to learn about the history of Ireland, its leaders, the language, music, poetry, dance, and spend time with its people! Truly an amazing opportunity! But what made the “craic so mighty” was the people whom I spent time with. By the end of the trip we all considered each other family. We lived together, studied together, traveled together, laughed together, and cried together. Not only the students, but our counselors as well! Taryn, Dan, Angie, Pete, Siobhan, and Brian (the coolest bus driver EVER!) made our trip an unforgettable experience! I will always remember my first visit to Ireland, and it most certainly won’t be my last. I highly recommend Irish Life Experience; this program broadened my knowledge and opened my eyes to the wonderful world we live in. I would like to thank everyone who was a part of ILE 2010 for being so amazing; you will never realize how much you mean to me! I miss you guys so much and love you even more!
-Hannah F., Elwood, IN-Student 2010
The Irish Life Experience was a complete and total refreshing encounter for both my daughter and I. As a parent, I was looking for an experience that was safe, educational and awe inspiring. I was looking for an experience that would broaden the mind of how awesome God and His creations truly are. I am not an experienced traveler, so additionally, I was looking for a way to build a comfort level for my daughter to safely travel within and outside of the USA. The ILE program exceeded my expectation on every level!
You were so helpful in answering all my questions about the ILE program prior to the application process. You were over the top helpful in arranging the non-stop connecting flights to and from New York. The updates and photos on the blog were exceptional. I don’t see any room for improvement…, everything was perfectly perfect!!!
-Mary F., Elwood, IN-Mother of Hannah 2010



I’m not about to write a bunch of cheesy things about how Irish Life Experience changed my life or anything, but I will say this: It was an incredible experience, one that I’ll be able to look back on in years to come with fondness. I spent months looking for the right organization to travel to Ireland with, and I’m confident that no other program could have given me the same kind of experience. With such a small group, we developed relationships which will last long after we left the Emerald Isle. I can think of no better way to see Ireland for the first time. It was the perfect mix of independence and structure, and I know that no other program could possibly have given me that experience. Having been a part of ILE 2010, I know that nothing can compare to that month I spent in Ireland getting to know people from all around the US at the same time as I traveled around the country I had been wanting to see for years. If I could do it all over again, I would.
-Joe P., Arlington, VA-Student 2010
We did a lot of research on summer experiences in Ireland. The Irish Life Experience was the perfect choice for Joe, who came into it knowing a lot about Ireland, its history and culture. The combination of a great itinerary and the relationships he formed with the other students, Irish and American teachers and staff added up to an extraordinary experience in this magical country.
We were doubly blessed to have Taryn and Sara at Tenon Tours help us with our own trip, meeting up with Joe at the end of his ILE summer and enjoying another week together. It was an unforgettable trip.
-Melinda P., Arlington, VA-Mother of Joe 2010


The Irish Life Experience was everything I wanted it to be and a little more. The first day we arrived, I had already had the most awkward conversation with my soon to be best friends, and I think the coldest shower I have ever had (that got fixed though). The first days in Waterford were full of fun and learning. We had our first experiences in Ireland: Petting a horse, finding a lady with a pram, learning of Siobhans Tayto’s obsession, and getting acquainted with everyone else on the trip. When I saw the different sides of Ireland, I came to love the fact that it reminded me of any where I have traveled before and the fact that it had its own personality. When you arrive in Ireland you can tell something is different about it, but it may have just been the strange Counselors (just kidding)! The Counselors (if you can even call them that) were amazing. Taryn, who worked hard to get us to the coolest places in Ireland with a smile on her face the whole time! Angie, who’s love for Irish literature, songs, and shopping made us love her. Dan who’s knowledge of history, and hilarious remarks kept everyone laughing. Siobhan who’s fun nature, and Irish Step Dancing kept everyone at ease. Pete who’s passion for Irish music and literature inspired everyone. Everything about the Counselors unique quirks made the trip a billion times better than I could have imagined. I made friends who I plan to stay in touch with and memories that I plan to carry forever. When I think of what an experience is…, I think of having fun, learning, loving, and having good company. So when I say that ILE was an experience, I mean it with the utmost sincerity.
-Savannah C., Suffield, CT-Student 2010


My name is Susan Keller and my daughter,Caitlyn Walsh, went to Ireland in July 2010. My daughter just turned 17 in June had never been away alone without a parent and never flew alone either. When we first decided to take this trip, I was really nervous. I had Taryn give me references of other parents and I must have called her many times. She was always so patient with me and I appreciate that. After the great references and speaking with Taryn, I felt comfortable with her going. When we were at the airport leaving, everyone who greeted us was so nice and so were the other kids going. My daughter had the time of her life! She always wanted to go to Ireland. They went to a lot of great places, learned a lot about the Irish culture and my daughter did grow up from this experience and she made some lifelong friends from all over. Thank you so much for taking such good care of my daughter, and the rest of the staff also. My daughter is already talking about going again next year. I will definitely be sending my other daughter. Again thank you for everything.
-Susan K., Bellmore, NY-Mother of Caitlyn 2010


These past few weeks have very likely had as strong of an impact on myself as they have had on these students, which began as an aggregate, quickly became a group, and returned home as a family. The only thing I enjoy more than spending time in Ireland is watching these students experience-with wide-eyed wonder-all the culture, history, and personality that Ireland has to offer. Angie, Brian, Dan, and Taryn have fostered each student’s adopting Ireland and now they will all bring a bit of Ireland back home with them. They will soon all be thousands of miles away from one another and this magical place, but with one song, one smell, or one memory, they will instantly realize they will always be in Ireland together, forever.
-Siobhan K., Winchester, MA-Student 2005, Counselor 2010



Friendships that will forever be cherished. Memories that will never be forgotten. An experience that has changed my life. I could sit here and write essays attempting to convey my feelings about the adventure I had in Ireland; however, there are not enough lines on a page or pages in a book or books in a library to express how grateful and truly blessed I feel to have been a part of such an incredible organization.
The Irish Life Experience not only assisted in my growth as an individual but also exposed me to an extraordinary country. Over this 24 day period, we learned a little Gaelic, brushed up on our Irish history, met the greatest people on earth, had talent shows, played games, spent a lot of money on souvenirs, toured the countryside, experienced city life, made scones, witnessed amazing monuments, climbed through castles, befriended other students from around the world, laughed until we cried, cried until we laughed, took over a gazillion pictures, swam in the ocean, had a scavenger hunt around town, studied historical and influential Irish leaders, learned how to play rugby, Gaelic football, and hurling, attempted to Irish dance, sang on the bus rides, biked around the Aran Islands, kissed the Blarney Stone, went to a concert, danced the night away in the discos, watched the crystal making process, had tea in the President’s House, took a Black Taxi Tour in Belfast, looked down from the Cliffs of Moher, saw the Leinster Gaelic Football Final, took a ferry from Ireland, went to a hurling match, painted artifacts, picnicked in the beautiful countryside, and traveled to over 20 different areas in Ireland in an effort to fully understand and appreciate the Irish Life Experience.
It seemed silly to put a price on making my dreams come true, which is why I knew I had to travel to Ireland and have an adventure. The people you meet will become family. The places you stay will feel like a home. Everything was perfect. I guess that was just the Luck of the Irish.
-PK C. (AKA Paddy), Chicago, IL-Student 2010
Many thanks to Taryn and the entire Irish Life Experience Staff for their dedication, care and hospitality during “the best summer” of PK’s life. We feel very blessed he had this incredible opportunity and sincerely appreciate the wonderful people involved in this organization. The detailed blog definitely kept us informed about the days events and the pictures were priceless. We would highly recommend this program and look forward to sending PK’s sister Erin there in the future!
-John and Lorie C., Chicago, IL-Parents of Paddy/PK 2010


I feel very fortunate to have traveled to Ireland as part of the Irish Life Experience. This was my first time away from home going away to a country that I had only heard about! Ireland is such a beautiful country so lush and green that it seems to welcome you with open arms. I learned so much about the culture and history of Ireland. The people were so welcoming and interesting. Every step of the way Taryn was there with her warm and friendly personality making the experience an unforgettable one. This was a once in a lifetime journey that I was so happy to be part of.
-Jocelyn A., Nesconset, NY-Student 2009
As a parent I was very pleased to be able to give this experience to my child. The Irish Life Experience was not your standard high school trip abroad. From the moment my daughter boarded that plane until she returned home I knew she was in good hands. She was in a safe environment with those who knew what they were doing. The culture and history classes combined with the field trips were an excellent way for the students to learn. This was a wonderful experience for my daughter. A special thanks to Taryn for all her help and support.
-Beverly H., Nesconset, NY-Mother of Jocelyn 2009


So, the summer of ’09 was by far one of the most memorable. Ireland. Who wouldn’t want to visit the land of the leprechauns? Traveling around the island was one of the most enjoyable times of my life. The experiences that I had were so much fun, and out of the ordinary for me. Mama T and Angie and Papa Dan were awesome chaperons and took very good care of their little ducklings (aka the ILErs of 09). It seems that the 24 days about the Emerald Isle really changed my personality and made me more mature. Basically, Ireland with ILE was amazing, I was seriously talking to another traveler scheming how we could go back.
-Eileen H., Alden, NY-Student 2009
Summer 2009, Irish Life Experience as seen through a Mom’s eye…
Eileen has returned home, safe and sound, with many new friends via email, skype and facebook. What is more important Eileen has returned home with a new viewpoint, maturity and appreciation of such a positive experience. Senior year is looming in the next few weeks and her summer experience has prepared her for impending life decisions. ILE provided the opportunity to gain some independence and see the world with just enough structure for a safe trip but enough freedom to explore her own interests. A special thanks goes to Taryn for her patience with all my questions, concerns and apprehension prior to the trip, even late arriving luggage was handled with a smile. Eileen is ready to return to Ireland but her ILE was more than just visiting another country, it was a stepping stone to her adulthood. It was a good parenting decision to share my beautiful daughter with ILE.
-Marilyn H., Albany, NY-Mother of Eileen 2009


This 2009 summer was by far the greatest summer of my life! I will never be able to forget all the great friends I made and all the amazing memories! Traveling around Ireland was incredible! Seeing the coast and all that the country has to offer was unbelievable. The teachers/counselors were the coolest people who made the trip so fun! I never wanted to leave!
Thank you Angie, Dan, Kendall, Pete, and Taryn!
-Caroline W., Skaneateles, NY-Student 2009


The summer of 2009 was the most memorable time of my life, and I will never forget it. I’ve always had a fascination with Ireland since I was little and have always imagined going there, but never thought it would actually happen. When I found out I was going I was estatic. The 25 amazing days in Ireland changed me as a person and my views on life all for the better. I met amazing people who I still keep in contact with and that I know will be life long friends. If I had the chance to go right this second, I would drop everything and be there in a heartbeat. Thank you Taryn, Angie, Dan, Pete, and Kendall for making this summer the best that I will ever have.
-Conor L., Richmond, VA-Student 2009


Taryn,
I just wanted to thank you, once again, for giving Cara a once in a lifetime opportunity to visit Ireland and her ancestry in such a warm and wonderful program. It was comforting knowing that she was with such a fine group of chaperons and counselors. Cara is the youngest, and last, of the children in our extended family to participate in this program. I’m only sorry that we don’t have any more to send! She began as a child that was very unsure as to whether or not she wanted to go on a trip where she knew no one. She came home as a confident young lady who talks constantly about going back and is in almost daily contact with one or more of the friends she met on the ILE. The experience was priceless!
Best wishes for your continued success.
-Eileen F., Farmingdale, NY-Mother of Cara 2009


I think the best thing I took from the ILE was the knowledge of Irish history, culture, and everything! Irish history is great for history buffs, culture is great for everyone, and the delicious food is great for carbon-based organisms! Everyone wins! I definitely believe this was the thing that made my summer the best summer ever [so far?]. I believe that the friendships we made are invaluable. I will never forget all of our crazy, fun buddies and the times we had together.
-Jordan S., Las Vegas, NV-Student 2009


To all of the prospective Irish Life Experience students out there- my one word of advice is to take this trip. Not only do you build strong relationships with incredible peers and counselors from all of the country, but you also have the amazing opportunity to explore an entirely new culture. This experience provided me with great friends and a lifetime of laughs. I am so grateful to have gotten this opportunity! This summer was by far the best of my life!
-Mary M., Bethesda, MD-Student 2009


Dear Taryn & the ILE Staff:
When my daughter Sophia asked to go on the ILE, I was excited at the prospects of her having a wonderful time abroad. I did not realize that she would engage in a life changing experience. Irish Life Experience is indeed an experience, an incredible journey for any teenager. In just a short time period on the ILE, Sophia learned more than just Irish history and Gaelic, she learned the importance of true friendship. She also learned to become independent and self sufficient. She has come back home truly enriched by this incredible journey. I can not thank you Taryn and the rest of the ILE staff enough for providing an opportunity for Sophia to learn valuable lessons that she will hopefully carry for the rest of her life. I highly recommend the ILE to any parent considering allowing their teenager to embark on this incredible journey.
-Melissa W., Gaithersburg, MD-Mother of Sophia 2009


Our daughter Grace participated in the ILE this past summer under Taryn’s care and had the time of her life! Her experience with the program was everything we had hoped for her and more. Not only did she get to see the beautiful countryside of Ireland, but she got to learn about Irish culture and history while making lifelong friendships with students from all over the US. We chose this program for our daughter because of our trust and confidence in Taryn. Our two older sons had been on a similar program to Ireland under Taryn’s leadership and we knew that Grace would be assured a wonderful trip if Taryn was in charge. Grace raves about Taryn and the other instructors as well as the trip itself. Thank you for helping our daughter experience Ireland and its people to its’ fullest and for helping her gain confidence and independence that could only be achieved by time spent exploring away from home. Our youngest can’t wait until he can participate in a couple of years! Erin go bragh!
-Mark & Susan M., Louisville, KY-Parents of Grace 2009


I went into the Irish Life Experience expecting just a memorable time, what I had was an unforgettable one. Although I was initially leery of signing away an entire summer, now I wish I could do it again a thousand times. I learned, grew, and made some great friends, all while touring one of the most beautiful places I’ve ever seen. Thanks Taryn!
-Jamie G., Dallas, TX-Student 2009
Hi Taryn, just wanted to tell you that this past summer was Jamie’s MOST AMAZING EVER!! Thank you for organizing such a fabulous Irish experience. As parents we really appreciated all the gorgeous online photo updates – they let us have a real window into his daily doings. Now when he talks about all his new friends we can find them in the pictures! We can tell how much he benefited from all he learned and experienced. His Irish grandmother is thrilled with his grasp of Irish culture and his entertaining tales!
-Melissa G., Dallas, TX-Mother of Jamie 2009


Irish Life Experience has been one of the greatest highlights in the lives of both my two oldest daughters. Both have returned full of wonder about Irish history, geography, culture and lifestyle. They have formed deep and lasting bonds with both the staff and students with whom they shared these experiences. They have returned more mature, wiser, and more self assured; and they are more confident to take on the role of world citizens and travelers. We are already planning for my third daughter to attend in 2012!

The program that Taryn, Angie, and the rest of the crew led not only opened me up to Irish culture and history, but most importantly enhanced my own life through Irish literature and music. To think of the life-long friendships which were formed during those dream-like weeks when I was sixteen in Ireland, it’s truly unbelievable. It inspired me so much that I returned six years later as a counselor!
I went to Ireland with Angie and Taryn during the summer of 2007. It was by far the best summer of my life. We spent almost a month studying and traveling and living with each other. I met my best friend on that trip, one who I still fly out to see today. The country was beautiful and I enjoyed every minute I spent in Ireland.
It was truly the experience of a lifetime.
Thank you Irish Life Experience.
-Katie L., Columbus, OH-Student 2007



From the moment you land, you are greeted by those who you are about to share an unforgettable journey with. Taryn and Angie were really helpful in deciding what was fun and available during the free time to experience Ireland the true way in becoming part of the culture. Everyday is a new adventure and in every adventure you meet new people and make new friends, which you will have forever. I still fly out to see my best friends in Ohio and New Jersey and even drive a few hours to see the ones close to home.
-Michael B., Joliet, IL-Student 2007


I had a blast discovering Ireland! Taryn and Angie made the trip fun every step of the way…even the classroom parts! I made so many wonderful new friends from across the country too! There are so many terrific memories from exploring Dublin on our own, to kissing the Blarney Stone, to walking across the bridge at Giant’s Causeway…I hope to go back someday.
-Ryan P., Mendham, NJ-Student 2007
We were so pleased with every aspect of our son’s trip to Ireland. Taryn and Angie made the entire process easy to manage and were always available to handle any questions. Their attention to detail and concern for safety, as well as fun and education ,gave us complete confidence that our son was having a great and safe experience. The ongoing diaries and photos that were posted throughout the course of the trip, gave us an easy way to feel like we were part of the trip and a terrific sense of how things were going. After the wonderful experience we had, we plan on sending our daughter to Ireland with Taryn and Angie as we know she’ll have a great experience and be in safe hands!
-Kathy & Jonathan P., Mendham, NJ-Parents of Ryan 2007


I would like to thank Taryn Harrison for the best experience my daughter Andrea has had. She traveled to Ireland with Taryn and Angie for summer program. I was so impressed with the organization, safety, and communication of their program. They communicated daily through internet and posted pictures. As a parent I was worried letting my child travel abroad. Taryn was helpful prior to Andrea leaving with multiple calls and e-mails.If anyone has any questions about this program please feel free to call me. My number is 781-536-8077. My daughter made life long friends that she keeps in touch with and is hopeful to return to Ireland in the future.
-Kathleen C., Boston, MA-Mother of Andrea 2007


My trip to Ireland was an amazing experience that provided me with many memories I will cherish for the rest of my life. It opened my eyes not only to the richness of Irish culture, but also to the vastness of my own country. I became close friends with people from all over the US and Canada who I still keep in touch with. Though we were only together there for a month, we shared experiences that bound us together forever. What truly made my experience in Ireland a special one, however, were the trip leaders. When I arrived at the airport I was greeted by Taryn, who already knew the names of every group member and made us all feel so comfortable and welcome. Both Taryn and Angie did an amazing job of exposing us to different aspects of Irish culture and fostering within us a love of Ireland as great as their own. Read more…

Living, studying, and touring Ireland for a month was simply incredible. I learned a lot about Irish history, culture, and even a little Irish dance! Taryn and Angie were both amazing teachers who inspired in me a deeper, more profound, appreciation of Ireland and its culture. Through my studies there, I grew to appreciate Irish music, and literature, something that would not have been possible if I had remained in the States. During my month in Ireland, I made dozens of friends with whom I speak and visit regularly. I can not think of a better way in which I could have spent my summer. I will never forget my tour of the Emerald Isle, nor the many friends I made. Thanks to all the hard work of Taryn and Angie, my summer spent in Ireland was simply extraordinary.

I feel lucky and blessed to have experienced a comprehensive and amazing trip to Ireland at such a young age. Traveling around the magical country of Ireland was the most enlightening experience of my life and Taryn and Angie made it even more enriching. My experience in Ireland taught me to embrace my heritage and be proud of where I come from. I felt right at home in while there and by the time I did come home a month later I knew so much more about The Emerald Isle because Angie and Taryn made it a fun learning experience. I could not have had a better experience in Ireland with them and would go on the trip again in an instant. Read more…
-Meghan B., New Jersey-Student 2007


My 16th summer was the summer that changed my life. The summer that I fell in love. Not with a person, but with my Irish culture and my heritage through the program that the staff of the Irish Life Experience led, which I was lucky enough to share with some of the greatest people I have ever met. Through this summer study abroad program, I not only learned about the history of my culture, or about the literature, but also about the people and how they live… One of the things that made my time in Ireland so valuable, were the counselors and the teachers that made me eager to learn, as well as explore the quaint cities we were situated in. Taryn and Vinnie encouraged us to try new things and to learn as much as we could, while Angie thrust us into Irish culture with her sharp wit and lilting brogue that brought the stories of Ireland’s writers to life for us. Read more…
-Maureen M., NY-Student 2007


Stepping off the plane in Ireland, I was a little nervous. I was 3000 miles from home and was with 70 people I hardly knew. I had nothing to worry about, though. Taryn and Angie were so welcoming and friendly that I felt comfortable in no time. Over the course of the next month, I experienced things that I will never forget. Whether it was touring the streets of Dublin or visiting the Aran Islands for the day, I learned so much. I remember the end of the trip and how sad everyone was that we had to leave. All of the participants had a great time that year. It was an once-in-a-lifetime trip that I wish I could do all over again! Traveling to Ireland with Taryn and Angie was a remarkable experience. I still go through my pictures from the trip all the time!
-Brendan P., Washington D.C.-Student 2006


I can point to the summer of 2005 as one of the defining moments of my life. It was the summer that I saw Ireland, the summer I was introduced to a beautiful country and its people, the summer that grew me so much as a young adult. Going to Ireland with Taryn was truly one of the most amazing experiences of my life! It was so exciting to learn more about Irish culture and history in class and paired with first-hand experiences through the various travels was the epitome of a perfect combination. I still keep in touch with the friends I made during my magical time in Ireland and we have flown to see each over the years! It was such a beautiful experience and inspired me to continue learning about other cultures and places!
-Kaitlin M., Chicago, IL-Student 2005


Sometimes a time, a place, an experience is so impacting that to think of anything before it seems impossible. I traveled to Ireland during the summer of my Junior year, and after that summer could honestly say that I’d grown up in Ireland – in so many ways I had! Looking back on that time, I realize it is possible to find family in new friends and feel at home when discovering a new place. Angie and Taryn fostered an all-encompassing experience, inspiring a love for both Ireland’s history and the contemporary culture. It is said that Ireland, once seen, stays with you forever – I will always remember how lucky I was to see and experience Ireland with Angie and Taryn.
-Aine K., Winchester, MA-Student 2002

title: Protected: Drama Presentations

content_raw:
On Friday, students had their last day of class and preparation for their drama presentations in the afternoon.  
The group of Eamonn de Valera did a Jeopardy skit for the students, the life of Charles Stewart Parnell was portrayed in an act of the Ghosts of Christmas Past and the two remaining groups of Michael Collins and Padraig Pearse acted out their lives. Eileen, Elysse, Sophia, and Cliff were in the Eamonn de Valera group and were treated to a nice sit down dinner at Gormet Burger Kitchen.  Congratulations!

title: Protected: Northern Ireland
author: studentblog
content_raw:
On Thursday was probably one of the most special tours of the ILE. The Giant’s Causeway, Carrick-a-rede Rope Bridge, and Ballycastle. Fifteen years ago, going up North would be unheard up, because of the Troubles. However, now ILE students were able to witness the beauty of the Antrim Coast.
It was a long bus ride, but as we passed through Belfast-with Angie pointing out her house-students began to notice the different flags in each town.  Some towns would have the Tricolor flying everywhere, even the curbs were painted green, white, and orange.  In other towns, the Union Jack would be proudly displayed.  “It’s interesting,” said Jordan.
With heavy rain almost the entire journey up to the Giant’s Causeway, we arrived and the sun began to shine.  Just our luck!  The Giant’s Causeway is an area of about 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, the result of an ancient volcanic eruption.  In a 2005 poll of Radio Times readers, the Giant’s Causeway was named as the fourth greatest natural wonder in the United Kingdom.  The tops of the columns form stepping stones that lead from the cliff foot and disappear under the sea.  Most of the columns are hexagonal, although there are also some with four, five, seven and eight sides.  The tallest are about 36 feet high.
Angie and Dan also shared the legend associated with the Giant’s Causeway.  Legend has it that the Irish warrior Fionn Mac Cumhaill built the Causeway to walk to Scotland to fight his Scottish counterpart Benandonner.  Fionn fell asleep before he got to Scotland.  When he did not arrive, the much larger Benandonner crossed the bridge looking for him.  To protect Fionn, his wife Oonagh laid a blanket over him so he could pretend that he was actually their baby son.  When Benandonner saw the size of the infant, he assumed the alleged father, Fionn, must be gigantic indeed.  Therefore, Benandonner fled home in terror, ripping up the Causeway in case he was followed by Fionn.
It was a perfect start to the ILE’s exploration of the Causeway.  We ate our packed lunches and watched a short video about the Causeway, before we decided to take a walk on the upper path.  It’s about a mile hike, with gorgeous views.  Students stopped off to take amazing pictures, before reaching the Organ and the Boot.  Students had about an hour climb on the rocks and take pictures.  “It was stunning, and I could have stayed there forever,” said Eileen.  
The weather managed to hold off the whole time we were at the Giant’s Causeway, but just as we were leaving to go to our next destination, Carrick-a-rede Rope Bridge, it started sprinkling.  That didn’t stop the students though from wanting to see more of the Antrim Coast.  We put on our rain jackets and took off the path to the bridge.  
Carrick-a-Rede Rope Bridge is a rope suspension bridge.  The bridge links the mainland to the tiny Carrick Island.  The site is owned and maintained by the National Trust, spans twenty metres and is thirty metres above the rocks below.  Today the bridge is mainly a tourist attraction, with 227,000 visitors in 2008.  The bridge is now taken down every year in late October or early November, depending on weather conditions, having been put up in March.  Carrick-a-rede means ‘rock in the road’.  It is thought salmon fishermen have been erecting bridges to the island for over 350 years. 
All of the ILE students crossed the bridge and some were definitely frightened by the height.  Jocelyn was especially scared, but made it across and back.  It was definitely worth the shaky knees, because the views were absolutely spectacular.  You could even see Scotland!
We definitely got our fill of exercise for the day, before stopping off in Ballycastle for dinner.  The students were given money to enjoy some of the restaurants around the popular seaside town.  Chinese, Fish and Chips, and Italian.  
With our bellies full, we left for our three hour bus journey back to Dublin.  Lots of naps, story telling, listening to music, and singing.  It doesn’t get any better than this!

title: Protected: In Dublin’s Fair City…
author: studentblog
content_raw:
On Wednesday, the ILE spent the day in Dublin…, and what a day it was!  We first started out at the Yeats’ Exhibition.  Through the National Library of Ireland, it explores the life and works of William Butler Yeats.  A very impressive display.  “Cast a cold Eye On Life, on Death, Horseman Pass By.” -W.B. Yeats.  
From the Yeats’ Exhibition, we couldn’t help but stop around the corner at the National Art Gallery in Ireland to see the Caravaggio’s-Taking of Christ.  A once in a lifetime opportunity for the students-even if they didn’t appreciate art.
We then decided to make our way to the Guinness Brewery-where we were able to tour all seven stories of the Factory.  Taryn was even able to start her own brew with her name on it.  So cool.  We stopped at the Gravity Bar for our free cokes, before we stocked up on souvenirs at the Guinness Storehouse.  
After all of our visits, we had a very important tour at the President’s House-Áras an Uachtaráin-in Phoenix Park.  With the students in their best dress, we were greeted by Keith Mulderry, who would give us the tour of the four bottom rooms of the President’s House.  Secretary to the President, Tim O’Connor, also stopped by to say hi, which was a special treat.  The ILE enjoyed tea and biscuits and were able to get some quality pictures.  Keith was an excellent host and we truly enjoyed his knowledge.  Plus, in the last room, River, Jordan, Pete, and Conor were able to play on the President’s Steinway piano.  Amazing!  Even though the President was in Navan with her family, most of the students agreed it was still well worth the visit.

title: Protected: Catching Up!
author: studentblog

I’m so sorry these posts are delayed, but we were having trouble with the internet at King’s Hospital.  My apologies.  Better late than never though:).  Enjoy!
On Tuesday, Teacher Angie read a Frank O’Connor story to the students and taught them about Seamus Heaney.  
Teacher Dan, taught the students about more of the 1916 Rebellion-which tied in perfectly with their tour of Kilmainham Gaol the day before.  He also had the students present to the class an Irish American they knew from home.  He was very impressed, especially by Caroline’s.  Caroline spoke about her grandfather and how he was a doctor for Kennedy.  Dan also taught body parts in Gaelic and prepared the students for Twister in Gaelic on Friday.  
Taryn gave out a quiz in her class and the students had to write down all of the counties in Ireland on a blank map.  Only four students received perfect scores-Catherine, Grace, Kelsey, and River.  Way to go girls!  They received very trendy Guinness pint glasses as souvenirs for a job well done!
The rest of the day was filled with a few workshops.  Angie held her famous Northern Ireland Workshop and talked about growing up in Belfast during the height of the Troubles.  She gave information to the students about both sides and shared her experiences.  It was very powerful and made the students feel very lucky that they would be able to go up North in a few days, because ten years ago, it wouldn’t have been possible!
A few students also took Taryn’s Celtic Frame Workshop and painted some beautiful masterpieces.  The students are so talented!  
Many of the other students had free time and during the evening we played a few games.  Scrabble has become a popular game with the students and the Staff.  Teacher Dan has become obsessed with Scrabble and will often challenge the students to a game or two.  Cailin has come pretty close to beating him, but he still holds the record for the most wins.

title: Protected: Fun Times in Dublin!
author: studentblog
content_raw:
On Sunday, the students were able to have a lie in.   They woke up mid-morning, got their packed lunches, and all got public transportation into the city.  They had free time to shop and walk along Grafton Street and Temple Bar area.  Many even went to see the Book of Kells at Trinity.  The ILE’ers are becoming more familiar with Dublin and are truly enjoying everything the big city has to offer. 
We returned back to campus after a few hours and had dinner.  Everyone wanted to go to the movies, so we took a trip to the cinema-many students seeing the new Harry Potter!  
After the movies, we thought it was important for them to see another Irish movie, In the Name of the Father.   In the Name of the Father, is about a small time thief from Belfast, Gerry Conlon, who is falsely implicated in the IRA bombing of a pub that kills several people while he is in London.  Bullied by the British police, he and four of his friends are coerced into confessing their guilt. Gerry’s father and other relatives in London are also implicated in the crime.  He spends 15 years in prison with his father trying to prove his innocence with the help of a British attorney.  It’s a great movie and appropriate, since we would be going to Kilmainham Gaol on Monday-which is where some of the movie was filmed.  Many students enjoyed the movie and said that it was interesting learning about more history of the Troubles.  A few said it’s also becoming easier to understand the Irish accents.  
Monday was the next tour of the program.  We went to Kilmainham Gaol first.  Kilmainham gives the visitor a dramatic and realistic insight into what is was like to have been confined in one of these forbidding bastions of punishment and correction between 1796 when it opened and 1924 when it closed and offers a panoramic insight into some of the most profound, disturbing and inspirational themes of modern Irish history. 
Leaders of the rebellions of 1798, 1803, 1848, 1867 and 1916 were detained here.  Such names as Robert Emmet, Charles Stewart Parnell, leaders of the 1916 Rising and DeValera are associated with the Gaol.  Two of the movies that the students have watched-Michael Collins and In the Name of the Father, were filmed at the Gaol.  One of the Staff’s favorite tours of the Program-it truly is moving and the students were able to piece more of of the puzzle together about Ireland’s history today.  
After Kilmainham, students had time to eat their packed lunches in St. Stephen’s Green Park, before boarding the Viking Splash Tour.  The Viking Splash Tour Guides are most engaging and amusing.  The students were able to wear viking hats and we all had to pretend people on the streets were Celts.  When we saw Celts, we had to let out a loud Viking ROAR!  It was a great tour to show the ILE around the sights of Viking Dublin City by land and by water, as the vehicles are also amphibious.  
When we returned back to King’s Hospital for dinner, we celebrated Angie’s birthday with a card signed by all of the students and a delicious chocolate cake.  HAPPY BIRTHDAY ANGIE!!! 
Counselor Pete had a fun activity planned for the students, so after dinner we had the Counselor Olympics.  Complete with wheelbarrow, spoon and egg, and dizzy bat relays.  The final competition was a water balloon toss.  Students were broken into their drama groups for the Olympics and the Charles Stewart Parnell team pulled off the win!  Needless to say, the winning team and Counselor Pete were pegged with water balloons at the end.  Ha!
What a great day!

title: Protected: How Do You Tell an ILE’er is Having a Good Time?
author: studentblog
content_raw:
They are Dublin over with laughter!  That’s right ILE Family and Friends…, we made it safe and sound to the nation’s capital.  Galway was absolutely incredible and all of the students loved every minute of their experience-some even got tattoos to remind them of all the fun they shared together in Galway.  HENNA tattoos that is, so don’t worry parents, they will wash off in a few weeks.  We are all looking forward to the next leg of our journey, so let the adventure continue. 
While it was a long journey from Galway to Dublin-with a quick stop for lunch in Athlone-the students were still looking forward to being set free on the streets of Dublin for a few hours for dinner and to explore the city.  
We said goodbye to our wonderful bus driver, Brain, and eventually got settled at King’s Hospital, which would be our home for the next week.  King’s Hospital is a Quaker school in Palmerstown, which is a 15-minute drive into the city center.  The very popular Liffey Valley Shopping Centre is a ten minute walk from the campus, so after students unpacked, they were able to stroll to the Mall and take a gander at some of the stores. 
They returned after a few hours, as we had a wonderful surprise and workshop for the ILE.  Angie’s brother, Tom,  and his traditional Irish band came from Belfast to King’s Hospital to play an incredible sessiun.  There were two banjos, a bodhran, a bouzouki, a fiddle, a flute and uilleann pipes.  It was simply amazing listening to all of the instruments together.  Lots of toe tapping and heads bouncing to the beats.  Two of the players were All-Ireland Musicians.  It was a treat for the students.   Eileen, Grace, Kelsey, and Kendall were able to dance a few reels while the band played-which was special.  Jordan and Tyler were not only able to join in with the sessiun on their fiddle and tin whistle, but were able to get private lessons!  Gemma (the fiddle player) and Paddy (the flute and uilleann pipe player) were extremely impressed with Jordan’s and Tyler’s natural musical abilities.   They both said that the two students were extremely talented.  
Before the sessiun ended, we challenged the students to a musical pose contest.  They had to pair up with a partner and dance their 3’s in a circle to the band’s music.  When the music stopped, one student from each pair had to sit on the other’s knee and freeze.  The pair that didn’t move and was most like a statue ended up winning.  It was a stiff competition between Cailin and Tyler vs. Cliff and Eileen, but Cliff and Eileen took the win!  Wahoo!

title: Protected: Moher of Ireland!!!
author: studentblog
content_raw:
On Wednesday, we left for our last tour on the West Coast-the Burren.  Our amazing tour guide and driver-Brian Farrell-is from Co. Clare-in the heart of the Burren, so it was very special as he shared his knowledge with us.  
The word Burren, comes from an Irish word-Boíreann-meaning a rocky place.  This is an extremely appropriate name when you consider the lack of soil cover and the extent of exposed Limestone Pavement.  However it has been referred to in the past as Fertile Rock due to the mixture of nutrient rich herb and floral species.  While the students learned that the rock in the Burren is limestone, they also were taught not to take it for granite!  Ha!
Throughout the day, Brian stopped at numerous points of interest for us and told many fascinating stories.  We passed through the beautiful seaside town of Kinvara, to an old Ring Fort, to the Poulnabrone Dolmen in the Burren.  A dolmen is a is a type of single-chamber megalithic tomb, usually consisting of three or more upright stones supporting a large flat horizontal capstone.  Most date from the early Neolithic period.  Dolmens were usually covered with earth or smaller stones to form a barrow, though in many cases that covering has weathered away, leaving only the stone skeleton of the burial mound intact.  It was very interesting for the students to see, as they were able to take pictures and walk around the tomb.
It was then off to Kilfenora-meaning Church of the Fertile Hillside or Church of the White Brow.  The small town is situated at the southern tip of the Burren.  Kilfenora is also home to many beautiful High Crosses, which students were able to see up and close.  The village also was the location of Craggy Island Parochial House for the comedy Father Ted and has the best clam chowder at Vaughn’s.  
We made a quick stop at St. Brigid’s Memorial, as the students were able to pay tribute and reflect on someone that they had lost in their lives, before proceeding to the Cliffs of Moher.  The Cliffs are 750 feet high at the highest point.  O’Brien’s Tower stands proudly on a headland of the majestic Cliffs.  From the Cliffs one can see the Aran Islands, Galway Bay, as well as The Twelve Pins, the Maum Turk Mountains in Connemara and Loop Head to the South.  The ILE spent an hour here and soaked it all in.  It was a majestic site to behold.  Plus, the weather was PERFECT!!!
The views back to Galway were absolutely stunning.  Brian continued to share his secrets with us about this incredible gem of Ireland.
After a long day of traveling, the ILE arrived back to Gort na Coiribe and prepared dinner.  All of the students had a buffet and each apartment provided a different dish-ranging from Spaghetti O’s, to Ramen Noodles, to french fries or chips, as they call them in Ireland.  
On Thursday, the students will be able to explore more of Galway on their own and discover the Galway Arts Festival.  We are excited!
Off to Dublin on Friday, so I’m not sure if we will have much access to the internet for a few days.  We’ll do our best to keep you up to date on all of our fun adventures.  I hope you have enjoyed reading everything so far.

title: Protected: Inis Mór Bound
author: studentblog
content_raw:
The island of Inis Mór-meaning the Big Island-is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Ireland.  Well known internationally, it is steeped in history and resembles an outdoor museum with over 50 different monuments of Christian, pre Christian and Celtic mythological heritage.  There isn’t far you can go before being somewhere where there’s something of historical interest and little reason to question its importance in modern Irish Culture.
This was our next tour while based in Galway.  On early Tuesday morning, we set out for Rossaveal and boarded the Aran Island’s Ferry.  After a quick hour journey over the calm seas we arrived Inis Mór and rented bikes for everyone.  The ILE was set free for the whole day to explore the Island.  
The island’s featured monument is the world heritage site of Dun Aonghasa Fort which stands over a dramatic 300 foot cliff that spans the entire western part of the island and faces the moods of Atlantic sea.  Others include the Black Fort set over cliffs, the seven Churches, St Benins Church perched isolated on a hill at the southern tip of the island,  Temphaill Chieran, and the old Light House at the islands highest point. Other places of a geological nature include the worm hole which is a large natural square hole in the ground  beside the sea, and the puffing holes where inland holes in the ground, fountain water on a turbulent day.
The weather held off for the majority of the day and most students were able to see one-if not more-of the island’s unique sites.  Some students even took a dip in the water and laid out on the beautiful white sand beaches.  
Today the Island features the Aran Jumper and celtic Arts and crafts such as Basket Weaving and Dancing.  Such is the culture of the islands 850 residents,  many people akin the daily rituals as going back in time where you can still find the horse and trap and hear the Gaelic language spoken as the first language and its consequent tradition.  A few of the students were even able to practice their Gaelic with some of the locals.  What a treat!!!
We got the ferry back at the end of the day and watched Father Ted on the bus back to Galway.  All of the students LOVED this tour.
When we returned to Gort na Coiribe, it was the girl’s turn to cook everyone dinner, so it was Mexican night.  Tacos, chips, and salsa.  Yum!!!
Some of the students also received wonderful care packages and letters.  Thank you ILE family and friends for all of the treats!

title: Protected: Well, I Took a Stroll on the Old Long Walk!
author: studentblog
content_raw:
Of a day -I-ay-I-ay, I met a little girl and we stopped to talk, Of a fine soft day -I-ay-I-ay, And I ask you, friend, what’s a fella to do, ‘Cause her hair was black and her eyes were blue, And I knew right then I’d be takin’ a whirl, ‘Round the Salthill Prom with a Galway Girl!     Galway Girl-Steve Earle
We arrived to Gort na Coiribe in Galway late Sunday night.  Taryn decided to make a CD for the students and everyone was able to pick one favorite song, so we listened to it countless times on the bus journey from Dublin to Galway.  The students were introduced to our incredible ILE bus driver-Brian Farrell with Burren Coaches-who would be our tour guide for the next week.  Parents and Friends…, if you are ever interested in doing a tour of the Burren, Connemara, or Galway while you are in Ireland-Brian is your man.  He’s one in a million!  www.burrencoaches.ie
We woke up early Monday morning with packed lunches in hand to start our first tour along the West Coast.  We first made a quick stop for a brief tour of the Connemara Marble Factory.  Connemara Marble is one of Ireland’s most original products.  Geologists estimate this natural green rock, quarried at the Streamstown Marble Quarries two miles northwest of Clifden, is about 500 million years old. 
Unique to the region, the marble shows twisted and interlocking bands of serpentine, in various shades of light green and dark green.  
Many students purchased a few souvenirs here for themselves, family, and friends.  They couldn’t resist.  
By the time we got back on the bus, torrential rain showers had begun.  We all began to hope and pray for a miracle that it wouldn’t be miserable weather for the rest of the day.  We decided to make a few brief stops for some gorgeous photo opportunities with the students.  Connemara is spectacular and simply breathtaking.  The low lying clouds, mist, and rain-gave the countryside that picturesque feeling.  The rolling hills couldn’t have been more lush.  We even managed to encounter an Irish traffic jam.  About fifty sheep blocking the road.  What a site.  
We pointed out the famous Quiet Man Bridge and stopped for a few minutes at the spectacular Kylemore Abbey.  Luckily enough, the heavens eventually broke free and the sunshine beamed down upon us, before we reached Dan O’Hara’s Cottage.  
According to local history the ruins of a cottage on the farm was once the home of Dan O’ Hara who was famous in song and story.  Dan farmed eight acres until he was evicted and forced to emigrate and ended up selling matches in New York.  
Martin Walsh and his family started started Dan O’Hara’s Cottage in the 1980’s to give tourists an insight into life in Connemara in the 19th century and the hardship endured by tenant farmers.  The ILE students learned about this…, and much, much, much more.  Martin was even able to show the students how to cut turf.  
After we learned a lot about the history, we were able to gather the students together for a quick game of horseshoes and tug-a-war.  
The horseshoe toss was very close, as Cliff and Conor ended up trying to win for both of their teams.  Cliff ended up with one more successful toss, so Team A pulled off the victory.  However, Martin couldn’t resist treating both teams to a box of Bailey’s chocolates for their efforts.
The tug-a-war was a little bit more interesting, as both teams were coached by Angie and Pete.  Pete told his team to play a little trick on Angie’s team and when he said “bananas” after pulling for a few seconds, his team let go, so the opposing team flew back and fell.  Everyone was in giggles.  Oh well!  
When we arrived back to Gort na Coiribe, students were able to go shopping across the street at Dunnes with their food per diem and make dinner.  All of the boys made dinner for the girls.  Spaghetti and garlic bread!  It looked delicious and was a formal event, as everyone dressed up.  Candles were lit and music was playing in the background.  You should have seen it!
What a great day with lots of memories to treasure!!!

title: Protected: Leinster Finals
author: studentblog
content_raw:
En route to Galway, we took a detour and stopped in Dublin for a few hours, as we were able to get tickets to the Leinster Finals for Gaelic football at Croke Park.  A very special experience, as it would be comparable to the Super Bowl in the US and tickets are extremely difficult to get.
Croke Park is the largest sports stadium in Ireland and is the headquarters of the Gaelic Athletic Association.  It has a capacity of 82,300-which made for an incredible atmosphere on Sunday with Dublin vs. Kildare.  Since Teacher Dan is from Dublin, he convinced all of the students they must cheer for his team.  Many students wore blue clothes and painted their faces before the game to show their support for Dublin.    
Our seats couldn’t have been any better, as we were directly behind the goal posts looking at Hill 16.  The students were able to see every play on the field.  We were very lucky! 
It was a very close game and Kildare almost pulled off the upset, however, Dublin came back to win it.  2-15 to 0-18.  UP DUBLIN!!!  
On our way to Galway, we stopped at a local shopping center and were able to get a bite to eat at the Food Court.  Many of us forgot that our faces were painted, so I’m sure we must have been an odd site to see wandering around the Mall.  Ha!  
What a blast we had!!!

Some more pictures for you to enjoy.  A few are from the Scone Workshop, which was a blast, but  as you can see…, the students were caked in flour.  We had a total of 36 scones to eat and share with friends afterwards.  They turned out well, but Jordan thought we needed to add more sugar.

Notice Cailin showing off her cross in the picture.  Kendall said that Cara had the best St. Brigid’s Cross.  Nice job Cara!
